intended_object: The Z-coordinate of the standard representative of the doubled point 2P in homogeneous projective coordinates on a Weierstrass curve: Z·(Y − negY(P))³ = Z·(2Y + a₁X + a₃Z)³. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body is Z·(Y − negY P)³, where negY P = −Y − a₁X − a₃Z. This is the standard projective doubling Z-coordinate Z(2Y + a₁X + a₃Z)³. The file confirms it with several lemmas. Around line 304, dblX/dblZ equals the affine addX for doubling. Around line 389, negDblY/dblZ equals the affine negAddY. dblZ_smul shows it is homogeneous of degree 4, consistent with dblU_smul. It vanishes when Z = 0 (point at infinity) and when Y = negY (2-torsion point, so 2P = O). The definition is stated over an arbitrary commutative ring, which is all the polynomial formula needs. The only other Mathlib definition of this kind, WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.dblZ, is for Jacobian coordinates, a different coordinate system, so it is not a counterpart of the same object.
